note: ECA Classic Modeler (eca_cm) is a core-only authoring UI for ECA. It implements ECA's EcaModeller plugin type with one modeller: @EcaModeller(id = core), class Drupal\eca_cm\Plugin\ECA\Modeller\Core. It defines no config, no permissions (reuses ECA's 'administer eca'), no config schema, no Drush. Models are ECA config entities eca.eca.<id>; create route /admin/config/workflow/eca/add/core. IMPORTANT for grading: in ECA 3.x the eca.eca config_export is only [id, uuid, status, weight, template, events, conditions, gateways, actions] — 'modeller' and 'label' are NOT persisted in that config (modeller is tracked at runtime via modeler_api). So execution/introspection cases are grounded on the eca.eca config entity's machine id and status, not on a modeller marker. Medium: enumerate model ids / read a model's status. Hard: create an eca.eca model entity (eca_cm_task) and enable a disabled one (eca_cm_toggle).

evals.prompt: I have ECA installed on a core-only Drupal site and want to build an ECA model without any external/BPMN modeler, using the eca_cm (ECA Classic Modeler) module. What path do I go to to create a new model, and what permission do I need?
evals.expected_output: Go to /admin/config/workflow/eca/add/core (the 'Add new Classic model' action on /admin/config/workflow/eca). It requires the 'administer eca' permission (provided by ECA).

evals.prompt: What kind of plugin does the eca_cm module contribute to ECA, and what is its plugin id?
evals.expected_output: It implements ECA's EcaModeller plugin type with a single modeller plugin, id 'core' (label 'ECA Classic Modeler', class Drupal\eca_cm\Plugin\ECA\Modeller\Core) — a modeler built purely on the Drupal Form API.

evals.prompt: Using the ECA Classic Modeler, after creating a model, what are the steps to make an action run when an event fires? What is the key concept that links components?
evals.expected_output: Add an event, then add an action (and optionally a condition), then connect the action/condition as a 'successor' of the event (at the bottom of the event form). Successor wiring defines the execution chain. Save to persist.

evals.prompt: This site has an ECA model configured. Inspect the live ECA configuration and give the machine name (id) of the ECA model that exists.
evals.expected_output: An ECA model config entity eca.eca.eca_cm_known exists (id eca_cm_known).

evals.prompt: There is an ECA model with machine id 'eca_cm_mod' on this site. Inspect the live configuration and state whether it is currently enabled or disabled.
evals.expected_output: eca_cm_mod is disabled (status: false in eca.eca.eca_cm_mod).

evals.prompt: Using the ECA Classic Modeler (eca_cm) on this site, create a new ECA model with the machine id 'eca_cm_task'. Apply the change to the live site so the model exists.
evals.expected_output: An ECA model config entity eca.eca.eca_cm_task exists (e.g. created via /admin/config/workflow/eca/add/core, or by creating the eca config entity with id eca_cm_task and modeller 'core').

evals.prompt: The ECA model 'eca_cm_toggle' on this site is currently disabled. Enable it so ECA will run it, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: eca.eca.eca_cm_toggle status is TRUE (enable from the ECA model list, or set status true on the eca config entity).
